title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 2, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: pydantic/pydantic-ai is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: pydantic/pydantic-ai leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: pydantic/pydantic-ai — 31 commits today, 7.7 above its current daily pace, with 18 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 138 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
earendil-works/pi — No same-day commit after 134 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Test whether recalled plans lead back to the user’s actual decision
dailyInsight.insight: Mastra has added navigation around recalled observation groups. An application can expose the surrounding record instead of asking the agent to answer from one search excerpt.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The October 1 change adds an observations recall mode, cursors across retained generations and guidance to confirm disputed details against original messages. Paging filters out reflection summaries; it does not recreate missing history.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: An assistant’s proposed date and a user’s accepted date are different facts. A navigable source trail gives the agent a way to distinguish them.

actions.label: Try a proposal-and-rejection fixture
actions.instruction: In a disposable application pinned to a revision containing this change, create a conversation in which an assistant proposes a date and the user rejects it. After observation and reflection, ask which date was agreed. Inspect whether recall pages the relevant observations and reads the original messages. Keep production memory unchanged.

receipts.title: Navigable recalled observations
receipts.supports: Explains the new search, observation paging and raw-message confirmation sequence and the proposal-versus-decision problem.

receipts.title: Observation paging implementation and regression fixtures
receipts.supports: Adds original-group paging across generations, thread filtering, retained-history boundaries and tests for the navigation contract.

confidence.basis: The merged implementation, retrieval instructions and regression definitions agree; the proposed fixture has not been run here.

dailyInsight.limitation: Source inspection does not establish a released installation or improved model recall accuracy. Retained observations can omit details, and navigation does not guarantee the agent follows the guidance.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A pinned reproduction in which valid retained groups cannot be paged or a source range leads to the wrong thread would contradict this implementation reading.
dailyInsight.watchNext: An end-to-end example showing a model retrieving a later user decision after an earlier proposal has been summarized.
